A Pod models an application-specific 'logical host': it contains one or more application containers which are relatively tightly coupled [v1.31:concepts/workloads/pods/_index#c0]. In non-cloud contexts, applications executed on the same physical or virtual machine are analogous to cloud applications executed on the same logical host [v1.31:concepts/workloads/pods/_index#c0]. As well as application containers, a Pod can contain init containers that run during Pod startup [v1.31:concepts/workloads/pods/_index#c0]. You can also inject ephemeral containers for debugging if your cluster offers this [v1.27:concepts/workloads/pods/_index#c0]. per_question_results.question: What does kube-scheduler do?
per_question_results.answer: In Kubernetes 1.27, and In Kubernetes 1.31, kube-scheduler is a control plane component that watches for newly created Pods with no assigned node, and selects a node for them to run on [v1.27:concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler#c2]. In both versions, kube-scheduler is designed so that, if needed, you can write your own scheduling component and use that instead [v1.27:concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler#c2]. It filters out any nodes that don't meet a Pod's specific scheduling needs and finds feasible Nodes for a Pod [v1.27:concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler#c2]. It then runs a set of functions to score the feasible Nodes and picks a Node with the highest score among the feasible ones to run the Pod [v1.27:concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler#c2]. The scheduler then notifies the API server about this decision in a process called binding [v1.27:concepts/scheduling-eviction/kube-scheduler#c2].

citations.quote: Kube-scheduler selects an optimal node to run newly created or not yet scheduled (unscheduled) pods.

Since containers in pods - and pods themselves - can have different requirements, the scheduler filters out any nodes that don't meet a Pod's specific scheduling needs.

per_question_results.question: How does a Deployment perform a rolling update?
per_question_results.answer: In Kubernetes 1.27 and 1.31, a Deployment performs a rolling update by updating Pods in a rolling update fashion when the.spec.strategy.type is set to RollingUpdate [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#c7]. The Deployment updates Pods in a rolling update fashion when the.spec.template is changed, such as by updating the labels or container images of the template [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#c7]. Other updates, such as scaling the Deployment, do not trigger a rollout and do not create a Deployment revision, allowing for simultaneous manual- or auto-scaling [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#c7]. When a Deployment's rollout is triggered, a new revision is created if the Deployment's Pod template is changed [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#c7].

citations.quote: Sometimes, you may want to rollback a Deployment; for example, when the Deployment is not stable, such as crash looping.
This means that the new revision is created if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (.spec.template) is changed, for example if you update the labels or container images of the template.
Other updates, such as scaling the Deployment, do not create a Deployment revision, so that you can facilitate simultaneous manual- or auto-scaling.

citations.quote: A PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) allows application owners to limit the number of Pods of a replicated application that are down simultaneously from voluntary disruptions.
A PodDisruptionBudget has three fields: - A label selector .spec.selector to specify the set of pods to which it applies.
This field is required.
- .spec.minAvailable which is a description of the number of pods from that set that must still be available after the eviction, even in the absence of the evicted pod.
minAvailable can be either an absolute number or a percentage.
- .spec.maxUnavailable (available in Kubernetes 1.7 and higher) which is a description of the number of pods from that set that can be unavailable after the eviction.
It can be either an absolute number or a percentage.

per_question_results.question: How do I set CPU and memory requests and limits for a container?
per_question_results.answer: Assign CPU Resources to Containers and Pods shows how to assign a CPU request and a CPU limit to a container [v1.27:tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource#c0]. Containers cannot use more CPU than the configured limit [v1.27:tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource#c0]. Provided the system has CPU time free, a container is guaranteed to be allocated as much CPU as it requests [v1.27:tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource#c0].

per_question_results.question: How does a Job track completions and what does parallelism control?
per_question_results.answer: When.spec.completions is specified, the Job is considered complete when there are that many successful Pods [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/job#c6]. Parallelism (.spec.parallelism) controls the maximum number of Pods that can run in parallel [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/job#c7]. For Jobs with a fixed completion count, the actual number of running Pods does not exceed the number of remaining completions [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/job#c7]. For Jobs with a work queue, parallelism controls the maximum number of Pods that can be created, and once any Pod from the Job terminates with success, no new Pods are created [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/job#c6]. In both cases, higher values of.spec.parallelism are effectively ignored [v1.27:concepts/workloads/controllers/job#c7].

citations.quote: - the Job represents the overall task, and is complete when there are .spec.completions successful Pods.

Actual parallelism (number of pods running at any instant) may be more or less than requested parallelism, for a variety of reasons: - For fixed completion count Jobs, the actual number of pods running in parallel will not exceed the number of remaining completions.
- when any Pod from the Job terminates with success, no new Pods are created.
Higher values of .spec.parallelism are effectively ignored.
